title: Outside the Cave
subtitle: Caves cannot shield all rain, nor can paper manuscripts.

content.text: Come here. Place your hand on it. Feel the texture. The craft is one of a kind, not some cheapie you can get from the flea market.
I mean it. This is a kilim, and even the most traditional, delicate, and expensive kind. It has applied fiery red as the dominant color, and the stitches are perfectly neat.

branch.text: From the sea, just like you, darling.
It arrived with a meerschaum pipe, a glass jar, a pack of sugar cubes, and a child in panic.
Both she and the kilim were born on the land where the craft originated. Their appearances apply the same dominant color, and the patterns in them share similar complexity.

Oh, your curiosity is aroused? But we are not done with the carpets yet. You've always gotta get a souvenir or two every time you reach a new place, so you will have something to show when you tell the stories one day, right?

Look at these handmade fabrics. How splendid ... Those incredible patterns were the only thing on the craftswomen's minds when they made the carpets. It's safe to say they have spent their whole life improving their skills at using the vertical loom, and that's how we get these carpet knots arranged in beautiful lines.
But they are just people like us. What if they get distracted? What if the carpet knots go off the right track and get tied to the wrong threads?
Then you will be in trouble, big trouble! All the problems in the universe will come at you, and the situation will be even worse than the bureaucratic system of a millennial empire.

content.text: Damn it! Damn it! DAMN IT!

branch.text: Calm down. Many swear like you do when there is nothing they can do.
They always step into the same river named Mistake again and again. That's why we need THEM, those crossing the river with their rulers, spanners, tool boxes, and dusty faces.

content.text: Can't we do something to fix it?

branch.text: I like the pragmatic quality in you. I'm sure it will make your life even more wonderful. The people will be impressed and line up to tackle the problems for you.
Oh, don't be mad. Some make troubles, and others deal with the troubles. That happens.
You know, every question has a questioner when they are raised. Likewise, every error has a corrector when they are corrected. That's how we get to know THEM.
The Correctors, an ancient profession.

Their duty is to remove the loose threads and iron out the wrinkles on the carpets. In the language of this island, that is to check the calculations on the papyri and even the holes on the punched tapes.

No one is capable of doing this job except the altruists, because it is similar to unraveling a ball of wool. Besides finding the end of the threads, you must always pay attention to the cats. Yes, the cats. They may jump on the ball and make things even worse.
And she, the red-haired little girl with the carpet in her arms, was overwhelmed at the beginning.

Not yet familiar with the ruler, she tried her best to find the end of the threads. So the cats took the opportunity to jump on her together and left countless scratches on that little forehead. Poor girl.
See, that's the problem every Corrector has to deal with: their job is to correct errors, but what if their own existence is also part of the errors?
Oh, it's no big deal. There is more than one loom in this world.
She left the complicated patterns behind and came to this simple kingdom featuring numbers only.

There she made the first contact with the spinning loom named geometry. She had never seen anything like that before, and it was almost impossible for her to comprehend how it worked. She could hardly convert the numbers on the books into an actual diagram in her brain.

Without a whole picture of what she was working on, she resorted to her hard work, and more hard work. Then a long time passed, leaving one wound after another on her fingers. Later, the wounds even became calluses.
In the end, her hands were no longer tender, but tough enough to resist the damage from the loom. Yes, she has won a place on this island for herself.

Yes, she's a quick learner. She learned even faster than some of the locals, but that was not enough, because she has been outmatched by her playmate, the leading one in the field of mathematics on the island.
That girl is like a perfect piece of satin born by nature. It is decorated by the beauty of mathematics and geometry, no manual work involved.
In order to reach the showcase where that perfect piece lies, and ... to stay on the right track and fit into the school ...
She has done everything she could.
But, BUT! She is still the most distinctive carpet there.
Anyone can tell that as long as they spend some time on the island.

content.text: It's not wrong to be distinctive.

branch.text: Of course not. She's only a bit "different" from others.
So she will continue to weave on the loom until one day the spindle pierces her callus and the fire burns everything to the ground.
Shh, I should stop here. You know that mathematician who was thrown into the sea? He died because he said something he shouldn't have.
Cut not wood on a public road; open not an unwanted bottle.
I don't know what to say next. I guess the best line for this circumstance is, "See you later."

items.text: Outside the Cave

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: I just saw it.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: The numbers of everything and every being would just emerge in front of me.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: I see it, and I speak it out loud. That's it.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: 210 told me numbers imply our fate.
37 frowns more deeply.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Don't believe him, Vertin! Numbers are just numbers. I know nothing about fate.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Hmm, fine. I don't think I like 210, and the feeling goes both ways for us.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Because I once said he is a poor number. 210 = 2 × 3 × 5 × 7. He is the product of all prime numbers between 1 and 10.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Looks like he has it all, but he doesn't have any real forte. He likes to sugarcoat himself with metaphors. Only those with a flawed essence would adore the trickery of words.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: This is indeed an extreme comment.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: And 6 is no better. Every leader of Apeiron has been a 6. 6 is the perfect number since it equals the sum of all its proper divisors: 1 + 2 + 3 = 6. But this number has been overrated. He's not that special.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: What about your number? What does 37 mean?

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: I don't know.
She purses her lips.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: I am 37. I've known it since I was born. So did everyone else.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: People told me what it means, but I have never tried to prove their theory.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: I know very little of fate, so I always think …

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Even if I find out their essences, does it mean I have known them better?

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: 37 once tried to tell me my number.
Sophia takes a deep breath.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: She wrote it down and put it into a bottle. But I couldn't get up the courage to open it. I didn't want to know.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: I once made a horrible mistake. An unforgivable miscalculation.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: It makes me worried ... that I may also be a mistake.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: So I threw the bottle into the sea.
She stops her patrol and turns back briskly.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: This is how 37 is different from us.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: We are all prisoners of that cave.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: Only the wise one can find her way out of the cave and return to rescue the rest of us.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: I'm the ignorant prisoner who sits, and she's the wise one who returns.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: I will be crushed into dust by the truth, while she will be the star shining above it.
Yes, she had heard the fable, but never quite like this version.
The red-headed girl lets out a sigh, raises her gaze out above the sea at the twinkling night sky.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: The truth is like the stars in the night sky—beautiful but cold.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: It has been there long before my existence and will stay that way long after I'm gone.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: It sheds no tears for the weak, nor laments the tragic fate. It's forever bright and always moving forward.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: The person who avoids the truth is not qualified to study it.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: I'm sorry. My interpretation has been emotional.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: No …

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: I think I kind of know how you feel, Ms. Sophia.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: However unworthy you think you are, there must be something we can do.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Maybe we can't reach the core of the truth, but we can clean up the path to it for the future explorers.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: This is our fate.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: Interesting insight.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: I have come to understand why 37 likes you so much.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: Let us go back to work then. Start from dusting the tombstones.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Alright, I've had enough of these soul, pneuma related idle topics.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: I wanna have a look at your model. Wow, seriously, how did you get this far?
Regulus eagerly pokes her head over. But 37 is faster; she has switched off the computer swiftly.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: This model has been proven wrong.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: For four whole years, we had been optimizing it.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: But the Emanation in 1929 only lasted for two days, which means our calculation was entirely a failure.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: That model is just like this computer. It's a piece of junk.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: And this is all I can present to you.
37 drops her head, looking sad.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: No, it's not junk.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I think I know why your model didn't work.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Wh-What?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Manus Vindictae has changed history.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: They accelerated history, forcing historical events to happen earlier than it was supposed to; thus, the "Storm" in 1929 occurred sooner than it should ...

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: No way.
37 stares at her in astonishment. Her shoulders shiver.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Controlling the Emanation? Changing the history of the outside world?

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Pneuma is eternal and transcendental. It won't obey any orders given from the phenomenal world. Neither will it change its patterns because of some fragments!

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I'm telling the truth, 37. I've been there, in the "Storm" of 1929.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Your model was not wrong. You just missed some key information.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: You've never been to the place where the "Storm" falls and thus know nothing about the symptoms of the Storm Syndrome ...

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: ... and the true purposes of Manus Vindictae.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: No! That's impossible!

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Even if there're means to control the Emanation, it wouldn't be like this.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: If this is true, does it mean the phenomenal world, this insignificant phenomenal world, is more transcendental?

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Mother's model was defeated by this?
She holds herself with a pale face, as if making a tough decision.
Eventually, she speaks up again with great difficulty.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Vertin, could you give us proof?

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: The proof that Manus Vindictae accelerated history and triggered the Emanation.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I swear I wasn't lying.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: No, not like this. To prove it in front of Apeiron.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Go to our sacred place, to the Hall of Truth, in the depths of the cave. There, everyone can see the essence of the world.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: I beg you. Give them your proof, just like how we submit the proof of our soul number.
TO BE CONTINUED…
